title: Magnetic behaviour of a spin-canted asymmetric lanthanide quinolate trimer

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, Dy(NO3)3·nH2O (0.548 g, 1.2 mmol, molar quantity calculated as the hexahydrate Dy(NO3)3·6H2O), 8-hydroxiquinoline (0.464 g, 3.2 mmol) and Et3N (0.14 mL, 1 mmol) were refluxed in acetonitrile (20 mL) for two hours to give a deep orange solution. The solution was cooled to room temperature and filtered. Orange X-ray-quality crystals of [Dy3(hq)7(NO3)2(H2O)] formed after two days of slow solvent evaporation. A non-equimolar amount of Et3N was required; an equimolar amount based on the ligand gave an insoluble product immediately, and no base gave a slurry.
synthesis.temperature: reflux, then cooled to room temperature
synthesis.time: 2 h reflux, then 2 days slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled to room temperature, filtered, and crystallized by slow evaporation of acetonitrile over two days to give orange single crystals.

properties.summary: The trimer is an SMM. χMT falls from 42.2 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature to 22.9 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K under 1 kOe because of crystal-field depopulation and intramolecular antiferromagnetic coupling. Zero-field AC susceptibility shows slow relaxation with QTM below about 5 K. Lines-model fits give antiferromagnetic Jlines12 = −0.07(1) cm−1 and Jlines23 = −0.27(1) cm−1, attributed mainly to dipolar coupling. μSQUID hysteresis is open at 30 mK and is strongly angle-dependent because the Dy anisotropy axes are non-collinear. CASSCF finds only Dy(1) strongly axial (gz ≈ 20, first excited Kramers doublet at 147 cm−1); Dy(2) and Dy(3) are rhombic with first excited states at 35 and 14 cm−1.
